title: The impact of mutations on TP53 protein and MicroRNA expression in HNSCC: Novel insights for diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
authors: Mahmoud, Ashraf Attia; Raih, Mohd Firdaus; Sage, Edison Eukun; Ali, Qurashi M; Suliman, Omnia H; Ibrahim, Sabah A E; Mohamed, Osama; Abdelrazeg, Samar; Mohamed, Sofia B
one_liner_zh: 该研究结合分子对接与分子动力学模拟，分析HNSCC中TP53错义突变对p53-DNA结合亲和力及复合物稳定性的影响，属于蛋白质-DNA互作机制建模，虽非典型TF-DNA结合位点预测，但方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系。
abstract: The tumor suppressor protein p53 (TP53) is frequently mutated in various types of human malignancies, including HNSCC, which affects tumor growth, prognosis, and treatment. Gaining insight into the impact of TP53 mutations in HNSCC is crucial for developing new diagnostic and therapeutic methods. In this study, we aimed to investigate the influence of mutations on the structure and functions of the TP53 protein and miRNA expression using computational analysis. The genomic data of patients with HNSCC were obtained from TCGA, and the impact of mutations on the TP53 gene was investigated using different bioinformatics tools. Results: The findings showed that the TP53 mutations increased TP53 expression levels in HNSCC and were associated with a poor prognosis. Furthermore, hsa-mir-133b expression was reduced in TP53-mutated samples, significantly affecting patient survival in HNSCC. Six mutations, including R273C, G105C, G266E, Q136H/P, and R280G, were identified as deleterious, carcinogenic, driver, highly conserved, and exposed. These mutations were located in the P53 domain, and PTM analysis revealed that R280G and R273C are at a methylation site, and R273C, Q136H/P, and R280G are located in the protein pocket. The docking research indicated that these mutations decreased the binding affinity for DNA, with R273C, R280G, G266E, and G105C displaying the most significant differences. The molecular dynamics analysis indicates that R280G, Q136H, and G105C mutations confer a gain of function by stabilizing the TP53-substrate complex. Conclusions: Based on the research findings, the mutations on TP53 were found to have an impact on protein and miRNA expression, development, survival, and progression of HNSCC patients, and has-mir-133b could be a promising novel biomarker for monitoring the progression of HNSCC. It was discovered that G105C and Q136H/P, as novel mutations, affect the function and structure of proteins causing HNSCC, which indicates that they could be interesting subjects for further investigation, diagnostics, and therapeutic strategies. Furthermore, the precise positioning of R280G and R273C within the methylation site and Q136H/P in the binding site has been documented for the first time. Moreover, the G105C, Q136H, and R280G mutations that stabilized TP53 structure and altered its interaction dynamics with substrates may serve as novel potential diagnostic biomarkers in cancer, guiding patient stratification and personalized treatment strategies. The molecular dynamics analysis provides insights into how specific TP53 mutations impact protein structure, stability, and function upon substrate binding, highlighting their role in cancer biology and potential implications for therapeutic interventions. This paper provides a novel understanding of the mechanisms by which these mutations contribute to the development of cancer.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤抑制蛋白p53（TP53）在多种人类恶性肿瘤中频繁发生突变，包括头颈部鳞状细胞癌（HNSCC），这影响肿瘤的生长、预后和治疗。深入了解TP53突变在HNSCC中的作用对于开发新的诊断和治疗方法至关重要。在本研究中，我们旨在通过计算分析探讨突变对TP53蛋白结构和功能以及miRNA表达的影响。HNSCC患者的基因组数据来自TCGA，并利用多种生物信息学工具研究了突变对TP53基因的影响。结果：研究发现，TP53突变增加了HNSCC中TP53的表达水平，并与不良预后相关。此外，在TP53突变的样本中，hsa-mir-133b的表达降低，显著影响HNSCC患者的生存。六个突变，包括R273C、G105C、G266E、Q136H/P和R280G，被鉴定为有害、致癌、驱动、高度保守且暴露的突变。这些突变位于P53结构域，PTM分析显示R280G和R273C位于甲基化位点，而R273C、Q136H/P和R280G位于蛋白口袋中。对接研究表明，这些突变降低了与DNA的结合亲和力，其中R273C、R280G、G266E和G105C显示出最显著的差异。分子动力学分析表明，R280G、Q136H和G105C突变通过稳定TP53-底物复合物而赋予功能获得。结论：基于研究结果，TP53突变被发现对HNSCC患者的蛋白和miRNA表达、发展、生存及进展产生影响，且hsa-mir-133b可能成为监测HNSCC进展的有前景的新型生物标志物。研究发现，G105C和Q136H/P作为新突变，影响蛋白质的功能和结构，导致HNSCC，这表明它们可能成为进一步研究、诊断和治疗策略的有趣对象。此外，R280G和R273C在甲基化位点以及Q136H/P在结合位点的精确定位首次被记录。此外，稳定TP53结构并改变其与底物相互作用动态的G105C、Q136H和R280G突变，可能作为癌症中新型潜在诊断生物标志物，指导患者分层和个性化治疗策略。分子动力学分析提供了关于特定TP53突变如何影响底物结合时蛋白质结构、稳定性和功能的见解，突显了它们在癌症生物学中的作用及对治疗干预的潜在意义。本文对这些突变促进癌症发展的机制提供了新的理解。
